replaces.basis: partially_sourced; envelope, power and price from the survey, mass a survey estimate

compute.placed: the chest tray, as build.py places a compute part

regulator.rule: the lightest of the catalog's 12 V regulators (JETSON_REGULATOR_OPTIONS; the carrier's DC jack takes 9-20 V and a 6S pack is at 25.2 V full, DECISION_LOG E7) whose rated output covers the dev kit's worst case at the jack in both power modes, since no mode is chosen: the mode's rail budget (power.COMPUTE_MODE_BUDGET: the module's cap plus 3 W of carrier, storage and cooling) plus the most the carrier can pass to its USB ports (JETSON_USB_VBUS_W), the carrier's own conversion loss left out.  The rated output is the catalog's power_max_w (12 V times the vendor's continuous current at its stated input voltage; the vendor gives a range of currents over input voltage and no figure at 6S, so this is the catalog's one point, not a rating at 20-25 V)
regulator.carrier_input_v: 9-20 V at the DC jack (compute survey: designlab/data/research/compute_2026-11-07.json, jetson_orin_nano_super_devkit); the catalog part's voltage_v is its own supply's 19 V

consequence.rule: what the rule's worst case costs in mass: on the modes' rail budgets alone (no USB load) the lighter option covers both modes (load_fraction_at_rail_budget), and the body would then be lighter by the two catalog masses' difference (lighter_option.body_mass_change_kg; with_reserve_kg adds the model's 6 % integration reserve).  Whether the worst case can occur at the jack is not sourced: the catalog does not give the rating of the kit's own 19 V supply.  If the power box already holds the computer's regulator (may_be_counted_twice), the body is lighter than modelled by the placed row with its reserve (placed_row_with_reserve_kg)

regulator.may_be_counted_twice: the power box's 0.30 kg is PR #662's power bay allowance, and that robot's bay held three regulators, a D36V50F12 for its computer among them (r0_posture_study_2026-11-07/study/hardware/component_basis.md); the bay's own breakdown is not in this repository, so the regulator placed here may duplicate one the box already holds: the body is then too heavy by at most the regulator's installed mass with its reserve
regulator.efficiency: the regulator's loss is in power.ETA_DCDC (0.88, A6), which every auxiliary rail takes; the vendor gives over 90 % for this part (catalog research record), so 0.88 is the lower of the two

pi_set.decision: leaves: the compute row (catalog part rpi5_8gb_ai_hat_plus_13tops, one part: the Pi 5, its cooler and the AI HAT+; its 0.100 kg leaves out the SSD) and the set's two power rows (pi5_ai_hat_plus, usb_ssd), which the dev kit's rows replace.  Stays: the compute tray's 0.12 kg allowance (NVMe, fan duct, mounts and leads: the build gives it to every compute part and resizes its envelope with the board), the 0.30 kg power box, the control stack and the IMU (the Teensy stays), and the 4 W MCU row.  The record holds no 5 V supply for the Pi and no SSD as items of their own (the catalog part's note names a 5 V, 5 A buck and a USB SSD; neither has a ledger row), so there is none to remove

not_placed.rule: not the baseline (owner decision P30: the microcontroller runs the walking loop and the CAN buses), so not placed and in no mass, centre of mass or screen of this body.  would_add_kg is the catalog mass times the count, and with_reserve_kg that plus the model's 6 % integration reserve: estimates of what the Jetson-direct option would add, with no position.  The catalog holds no supervisor part, so no mass is given for one

com_at_pick_pose_m.note: both bodies at the pick's home pose; from_parts: the pick's mass and centre with the changed ledger rows' masses and first moments exchanged

com_ahead_of_hip_m.note: change: each body at its own home (two stances); change_at_pick_pose: the Jetson body at the pick's home (home_pose)

home_pose.rule: the build solves the stance for the body as built (pipeline.build_candidate: statics.solve_stance shifts the feet fore and aft so that the centre of mass is centred over the support, the trunk pose fixed), so the Jetson body's home is not the pick's: the legs' joints differ (joint_change_rad) and against_base and com_ahead_of_hip_m's change compare two stances, the changed parts with the re-solved stance.  against_base_at_pick_pose and com_ahead_of_hip_m's change_at_pick_pose compare the Jetson body posed at the pick's home with the pick: the changed parts alone, as sizing.requirements reads them from that pose

jetson.rule: at the home pose, with the clearance screen's geoms and distance oracle (clearance._Screen): gaps_mm, the signed distance of each listed pair of trunk hardware boxes (negative: they intersect; a box inside its own envelope, as the compute board in its tray, reads negative and is counted under nested_envelopes); nearest_other_body, the closest screened geom of another rigid body (a leg, the head, the tail) to each item; same_body_component_overlaps, the screen's own reading behind its component_overlap_free gate; and trunk_profile_margin_mm, each item's corners against the as-built trunk profile with the build's 8 mm + 2 mm allowance (Design.profile_margin; positive: inside).  The trunk's own covers are not paired with its hardware: the screen's cover pieces are convex hulls that contain it.  The walking gates read the moving pairs over the walks (the case's clearance screen)

base.rule: at the home pose, with the clearance screen's geoms and distance oracle (clearance._Screen): gaps_mm, the signed distance of each listed pair of trunk hardware boxes (negative: they intersect; a box inside its own envelope, as the compute board in its tray, reads negative and is counted under nested_envelopes); nearest_other_body, the closest screened geom of another rigid body (a leg, the head, the tail) to each item; same_body_component_overlaps, the screen's own reading behind its component_overlap_free gate; and trunk_profile_margin_mm, each item's corners against the as-built trunk profile with the build's 8 mm + 2 mm allowance (Design.profile_margin; positive: inside).  The trunk's own covers are not paired with its hardware: the screen's cover pieces are convex hulls that contain it.  The walking gates read the moving pairs over the walks (the case's clearance screen)

loads_between_stances.rule: the largest change between the two stances (against_base, against_base_at_pick_pose) of a group's ratio to its drive's limits, and of a hold or RMS torque (relative, those of at least the floor): the sizing's holds and walks re-centre the centre of mass over the support from whichever home they start, so the re-solved stance moves the loads only this much, while the centre of mass at home moves with it (com_ahead_of_hip_m)

power_modes.rule: power.walking_power(design, requirements, the nominal walk's motor series, compute_mode) and power.runtime(pack, total): the record's own power and runtime method, the dev kit's row replaced by the mode's (power.COMPUTE_MODE_BUDGET); drives, MCU, sensors, the 0.88 converter and the 75 % usable energy as in every record

record_default.rule: the record's own power and runtime: power.COMPUTE_BUDGET's row for the dev kit, round one's 31 W allowance (A13), above either mode's budget

survey_typical_15w.rule: for comparison, not a mode budget and not a measurement in the 15 W mode: the compute survey's typical figure for this architecture, 12 W at the module plus the same 3 W of carrier, storage and cooling (designlab/data/research/compute_2026-11-07.json, A_orin_nano_super_devkit: 'Typical 15.0 W').  The 12 W was measured with locked MAXN SUPER clocks under a heavier detector load (arXiv 2609.13551), and the survey has no measurement in the 15 W mode ('No light-load measurement exists in the 15 W mode').  The base's row is a typical draw too (A14).  First order: the 15 W mode's result with the rail's difference taken off through the converter

heat.note: no thermal model of the chest, the electronics or the air path exists in this study; the drives' heating is read only through their sustained-torque ratios (the envelope screen's session_heat).  The dev kit's 15-25 W module (18-28 W at the rail) against the Pi set's 8-9.5 W, in a closed chest, is an open hardware question

selection_if_resized.rule: one step of sizing.select on these loads with the case's headroom, and power.select_battery on its walking power (the record's own, and each power mode's): recorded only (the sizing loop, which would iterate on the re-selected parts' masses, is not run, and nothing here is re-selected)
